Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The claimants in M.V.C. No. 366/2020 on the file of the MACT At Bagalkot are impugning the judgment and award dated 03.09.2022 awarding compensation of Rs.11,15,000/- with interest at 6% pa. from the date of petition till realisation.
Parties shall be referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
2. Brief facts of the case are that the claimants being the mother and brother of the deceased Deviprasad Angadi have filed the claim petition seeking compensation for his death.

It is stated that the deceased was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing no. KA-29/F-9491 as a pillion rider and at that time a lorry bearing reg. no. MH-10-Z-4025 came in a rash and negligent manner and in high speed from the opposite direction, dashed to the motorcycle, as a result of which the pillion rider sustained fatal injuries and died at the spot.
It is stated that the deceased was working as a Clearner and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
The claimants are depending on his income and are entitled for compensation.
Accordingly, they prayed for allowing the claim petition.
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle has not contested the matter.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the trial Court, denied the contentions taken by the claimants while admitting the coverage of insurance to the lorry in question.
3. On the basis of these pleadings the trial Court framed the following issues.

1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 30.11.2019 at about 5.00 a.m. near Kutakaneri Cross on Badami-Kendur road, while deceased Deviprasad was proceeding on motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-29/V-9491 as a pillion rider, met with an accident due to rash and negligent act of driver of lorry bearing registration No. MH-10/Z-4025 and succumbed to injuries on the spot?
2. Whether respondent No.2 proves the contributory negligence of rider of motorcycle bearing registration No. KA- 29/V-9491 involved in the accident as contended in para no. 3 and 5 of their written statement?

2 3.
Is the petitioners entitled for compensation, as sought for in the petition?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
4.
What order
or award?

Claimant no.1 is examined as PW1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 6 in support of their contention.
Respondent No.3 got examined PW1 and got marked Exs.R.1 and R2 in support of its contention.
The Tribunal after taking into consideration all these materials on record awarded Rs.11,15,000/-
with interest at 6% p.a. from the respondent nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally.
The claimants are impugning the judgment and award seeking enhancement of compensation.

4. I have heard Sri Chandrashekhar M. Hosamani, learned counsel for appellant and Sri S.S.
Koliwad, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the accident had occurred on 30.11.2019.
The claimants are the mother and brother of the deceased.
They were depending on the income of the deceased.
The Tribunal has taken into consideration income of the deceased at only Rs.10,000/- per month.
The income which the deceased was getting was much more than that.
Therefore, enhanced compensation amount is to be awarded.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that in the absence of any proof of income of the deceased the Tribunal has taken into consideration a reasonable amount and awarded as compensation which does not call for any interference and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

7. The point that arises for consideration in this appeal is:
Whether the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal requires interference by this Court?
8. My answer to the above is in the affirmative for the following REASONS 9.
It is stated that the deceased was working as a Cleaner and was aged 20 years.
Even though the brother the claimant no.2 cannot be considered as a dependant on the deceased, claimant no.1 being the mother, is the dependent and therefore she is entitled for compensation.
10. It is stated that the claimant was working as a Cleaner.

In the absence of any proof of his income the guidelines to determine the compensation before the Lok Adalath is to be taken into consideration, according to which during the year 2019 the income of the person is to be taken at Rs.13,250/- per month.
Since the deceased was a bachelor 50% has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
The appropriate multiplier is '18'.
Hence, the claimant no.1 being the mother
is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,31,000/- towards loss of dependency.
She is also entitled for compensation towards consortium at Rs.44,000/-, loss of estate and funeral expenses at Rs.33,000/-.
Smt Sangamma W/O. Shivanand Angadi vs Sri Santosh S/O. Ganapati Jagatap on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55172300/
3 11. The claimant no.1 being the mother of the deceased, is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.15,08,000/- as against Rs.11,15,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
12. In view of the above, I answer the point for consideration 'partly in the affirmative' and proceed to pass the following order.
ORDER Appeal filed by the appellant is allowed in part.

Impugned judgment and award dated 03.09.2022 passed in M.V.C. No. 366/2020 on the file of the MACT At Bagalkot is modified holding that the claimant No.1 being the mother of the deceased is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,08,000/- as against Rs.11,15,000/- awarded by the Tribunal with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation.
Respondent No.2 Insurer is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount along with up to date interest within two months from the date of preparation of the award.
Draw decree accordingly.
Send back the trial Court records along with a copy of the judgment and award.
